rows.grounds: instrument by which the rite is performed; refers to the mūla mantra
compound specifying the count: śata (hundred) + pañcāśat (fifty) + daśa (ten) + saṃkhyā (number)
presents an alternative to the previously stated procedures
the officiating teacher performing the ritual acts

items.question: What alternative mantra count may the guru use to perform the prescribed ritual acts?
premises: The guru is the agent performing the ritual acts.
The root mantra may be employed as the instrument.
An alternative count of one hundred sixty repetitions is specified.
items.inference: Therefore, the guru may alternatively perform the prescribed acts using the root mantra one hundred sixty times.
uncertainties: Whether this count applies to each act mentioned previously or to the procedure as a whole is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Or the guru may perform it with the root mantra, repeated one hundred and sixty times.
